transcript: My mother began studying English at 60, having been a homemaker for many years. She made the decision when her grandchild was born. At first, she struggled even with pronunciation Trying to make sounds, her mouth was not used to She would stretch her lips again and again She patiently corrected herself from reading tap as tapoo But my mother was determined She would get up at six every morning And listen to English lessons on the radio After breakfast, she would read the textbook For an hour, committing the words to memory After half a year, she could handle simple daily conversation After a year, she gave directions to a tourist After three years, she wrote an English essay at a university extension course My mother's progress was somewhat slow but steady The secret was, keep doing it every day Even a short amount of time continued for 365 days Becomes a vast sum of hours When her grandchild turned five She began speaking English with him The grandchild was amused To see his grandmother speak English Then he too began learning English My mother's story teaches me something important, too late is only an excuse If the desire to learn is real, one can begin at any age Modern society imposes the pressure on young people that you must work hard while young But in an age where people live to a hundred, learning is a lifelong pursuit My mother is 65 this year, she is now planning her first solo trip abroad The destination is London To make her own way through the world in English That is her new dream

segments.text: My mother began studying English at 60, having been a homemaker for many years.
She made the decision when her grandchild was born.
At first, she struggled even with pronunciation Trying to make sounds, her mouth was not used
to She would stretch her lips again and again
She patiently corrected herself from reading tap as tapoo
But my mother was determined She would get up at six every morning
And listen to English lessons on the radio After breakfast, she would read the textbook
For an hour, committing the words to memory After half a year, she could handle simple
daily conversation
After a year, she gave directions to a tourist
After three years, she wrote an English essay at a university extension course
My mother's progress was somewhat slow but steady
The secret was, keep doing it every day
Even a short amount of time continued for 365 days
Becomes a vast sum of hours
When her grandchild turned five
She began speaking English with him
The grandchild was amused
To see his grandmother speak English
Then he too began learning English
My mother's story teaches me something important, too late is only an excuse
If the desire to learn is real, one can begin at any age
Modern society imposes the pressure on young people that you must work hard while young
But in an age where people live to a hundred, learning is a lifelong pursuit
My mother is 65 this year, she is now planning her first solo trip abroad
The destination is London
To make her own way through the world in English
That is her new dream
